campaign.title: Prescribed-point persistence, local moment, and integer exceptional-set bridge

resource_policy.literature_policy: Audit only primary short-interval, large-value, or local Gauss-circle sources whose exact variable, interval, coefficient, and pointwise scope can be mapped. Structural analogy is not theorem applicability.

frozen_target.question: Starting only from the accepted global real mean square, prove the exact one-sided persistence and discrete exceptional-set consequences, then determine and attack the weakest uniform short-window actual-coefficient moment that would upgrade a prescribed point to the quarter exponent.
frozen_target.reference_formula: If M=|P(x)|, monotonicity gives M^2*min(H,M/(2*pi)) << sup_(|I|=H) int_I|P|^2. Audit whether the standard local scale H Y^(1/2+epsilon) for H=Y^(1/4+o(1)), or the stronger total scale Y^(3/4+epsilon) on a fixed longer window, can be proved from the literal moving M1/M2 expansion; otherwise isolate the exact signed rational-frequency cluster survivor.
quantities: Round-93 global moment int_Y^(2Y)|P(t)|^2 dt << Y^(3/2+epsilon)
local bridge M << Q^(1/3)+(Q/H)^(1/2) for local mass Q
top denominator D=Y^(1/2) and actual height |h|<<D Y^(-1/4)
scope: retain the jump convention and both persistence signs
derive integer and one-separated exceptional counts with bounded overlap
retain exact rational lifts, chi_4, both signs, floors, moving heights, hard top, stars, M1/M2 ownership, and R5 in every local expansion
do not infer a prescribed-point theorem from global Chebyshev
do not assume either canonical core or claim a uniform exponent without the signed cluster estimate

completion_criteria: Prove or refute exact one-sided persistence at all real and jump points.
Prove the one-separated sampling and integer exceptional-set consequences.
Derive the sharp local-moment-to-pointwise formula, including additive errors and boundary windows.
Decide whether unit-window local L2 is equivalent to pointwise control.
Derive the exact short-window moving M1/M2 frequency-cluster kernel.
Quantify the top-scale spacing capacity against the required local target.
Prove a nontrivial local range or name the first exact signed cluster survivor.
Audit current primary short-interval and large-value sources literally.
Complete clean blind, construction, and hostile/source gates.

tasks.target: Independently prove or refute the persistence, one-separated sampling, integer exceptional-set, and local-moment implication package, and identify the strongest conclusion available from the global moment alone.
excluded_context: all prior reports, candidates, reviews, syntheses, source cards, and sibling Round-94 reports
required_output: A full proof or exact first failure for every bridge statement, with no local-frequency claimant context.

tasks.target: Derive the literal short-window moving M1/M2 Gram kernel and try to prove the target local moment on H=Y^(1/4+sigma); if it fails, isolate the smallest exact signed cluster inequality and quantify every exponent.
required_output: An exact local kernel, a proved range or first signed survivor, exponent ledger, and graph-ready state recommendation.

tasks.target: Try to break every persistence, sampling, local-moment, endpoint, and implication normalization; audit primary short-interval or large-value sources and decide whether any literal theorem beats the top-scale cluster barrier.
required_output: A hostile seam table, literal primary-source map, sharp controls, and a promote/revise/reject recommendation.

review_seams.requirement: Check both signs, inclusive jumps, orientation, and dyadic boundaries exactly.
Prove bounded overlap for one-separated points and state the integer exceptional exponent.
Derive the local-to-pointwise and additive-error exponents without suppressing H.
Retain the exact moving coefficients and derive the frequency-cluster Gram kernel and tails.
Audit D=Y^(1/2), H=Y^(1/4+sigma), floors, hard top, and stars.
Separate almost-all integers from a prescribed integer and local equivalence from an actual local estimate.
Map every primary theorem in its literal variable, interval, smoothing, coefficient, and uniformity range.
